newsitem.title: ALBANIA: U.N. readies food for distribution in Albania.
newsitem.headline: U.N. readies food for distribution in Albania.

text.p: A U.N. food agency was making final preparations on Saturday to distribute emergency food aid to Albanian hospitals and orphanages as more troops landed from a multinational security force.
The U.N.'s World Food Programme planned to hand over wheat flour, beans and vegetable oil to hospitals, orphanages and homes for the elderly and handicapped, officials said.
The relief operation is running in parallel with diplomatic efforts to steer the Balkan country towards early elections in June and end weeks of violent unrest which have cost some 300 lives.
King Leka I, back in Albania after a life spent in exile, said on Friday he had won a promise from President Sali Berisha to hold a referendum on restoring the monarchy.
"The situation that has been created in the country needs a stabilising factor and I think in me they see a stabilising factor," the 58-year-old king said of his countrymen.
Albania, which emerged only this decade from half a century of isolation and hardline Stalinist rule, has plunged into chaos since the collapse of fraudulent investment schemes earlier this year.
The Geneva-based International Committee of the Red Cross, which does not use armed escorts, has so far handed out 50 tonnes of food -- a third of it in the past week -- and two tonnes of medicines.
But the pace of the humanitarian aid effort was set to pick up sharply as convoys of soldiers criss-crossed the country from an eight-nation security force led by Italy.
Some two dozen Greek and Italian armoured vehicles carrying at least 200 soldiers headed towards the rebel-held south, witnesses said.
They stopped near the town of Fier, just short of the crossing into an area controlled by so-called "national salvation committees," which reject the authority of Berisha.
The rebels blame the president for the investment scams in which many Albanians had invested their life savings.

More than 1,000 French, Italian and Greek troops from the security mission reached the western port of Durres and a reporter later saw a long column of some 30 Italian military trucks and armoured cars heading south. Its destination was not known.
The troops landing in Durres brought hundreds of armoured personnel carriers and tanks. More than 2,500 soldiers have arrived in Albania since the start of Operation Alba (Dawn) earlier this week.
"I could cry to see so many tanks, trucks and soldiers in my country," said a 39-year-old Albanian woman named Sabrie, who watched the troops march into Durres. "I know they are going to help us."
